headline: Granted a variance for an attached three-vehicle garage at 50 Wimbledon Circle and a six-month extension for 1122-1130 Main Street.
summary: Granted a six-month extension for Case No. 2023-18 at 1122-1130 Main Street. Granted a variance for Case No. 2026-21 at 50 Wimbledon Circle to build an attached three-vehicle garage at the rear of the home. The added conditions cover removing structures from City of Cambridge property, a property survey, and cooperation on boundary markers.
decisions: Granted a six-month extension for Case No. 2023-18 at 1122-1130 Main Street, 5-0 by roll call.
Adopted the Proposed Findings of Fact for Case No. 2026-21 at 50 Wimbledon Circle as the board's Findings of Fact, 5-0 by roll call.
Granted the variance for Case No. 2026-21 at 50 Wimbledon Circle with three added conditions, 5-0 by roll call.

On motion of Mr. Taranto, seconded by Ms. Gelineau, the board voted that the Proposed Decision, as amended tonight, be the decision of the board. ... Mr. Sergi: It's been granted.

plain_text:
City of Waltham 
Zoning Board of Appeals 
August 25, 2026 
The Zoning Board of Appeals held a public hearing at 7:00 P.M. on Tuesday, August 
25, 2026 in the Auditorium of the Arthur Clark Government Center, 119 School Street, 
Waltham, MA. 
In attendance were John Sergi, Chair, and members Matt Deveaux, Glenna 
Gelineau, Stephen Taranto and Joseph Attardo. 
Mr. Sergi: Tonight we have one new case and a continuation request. 
The first order of business tonight is to approve the minutes of August 18, 2026. 
May I have a motion to approve the minutes of August 18, 2026 please. 
On motion of Mr. Deveaux, seconded by Mr. Attardo, the board voted to approve 
the minutes of August 18, 2026. 
Mr. Sergi: So we have approved the minutes of August 18, 2026. 
Why don't we do the continuation case first, Case No. 2023-18, 1122-1130 Main 
Street. I hope Counsel you have a good reason for being here again with this case. 
Attorney Bret Francis, Law Office a 10 Hammer Street, Waltham came forward. As 
you indicated, this is my client's third or fourth extension which is also on top of the 
previous owner's extension. But that being said, since February when that extension was 
granted he's done a lot of work. He's had to go to Historic Commission. He's done all the 
other work. He's actually filed the application with the Building Department and we are 
1
waiting for the bnilding permit issuance. So we thought by now, I mean, this letter was 
drafted on July 24, 2024. His application to the building department was filed before that. 
So, he's still waiting on it. You Imow, at this point there's nothing else that we can do. We 
filed it over a month ago. This is just a precautionary measure to make sure that for any 
reason he's not denied the permit because of some extension. 
Mr. Sergi: I'm not happy to see it here again. 
Mr. Francis: I understand. 
Mr. Sergi: It just keeps coming for one reason or another. I'll open it up to the 
board before I comment. I am not happy about it. 
Steve, do you have any comments? 
Mr. Taranto: Not at this time. 
Mr. Sergi: Glenna: 
Ms. Gelineau: No. 
Mr. Sergi: Matt? 
Mr. Deveaux: He said final extension. Final extension is final extension. 
Mr. Francis: I mean again, it wasn't for a lack of effort. He filed in July no less. It 
wasn't like he filed the day before the meeting. He filed more than a few weeks before the 
deadline and he called me to file this extension. I said, you know, if you're not filed, there's 
no reason to go, I'm not doing that. 
2
Mr. Sergi: Give us some background again. He's been here so many times. What 
has he filed? He's filed the demolition permit, what's - - -
Mr. Son Le, 1122-1130 Main Street, Waltham: So, I filed for a demolition permit 
and construction permit and I have not heard back from either. I filed earlier in July for a 
demolition and then on July 22nd for the construction and it's been over thirty days since I 
applied so I'm assuming they are swamped in the building department. I haven't heard 
anything back about if I'm missing anything or what they want or any additional 
information they need in terms of progress at this point. 
Mr. Sergi: What are you planning? What's the construction that you are doing? 
Mr. Son Le: It's the demolition of a two family and we are going to be putting up a 
five family unit. 
Mr. Sergi: Oh, okay. Is that the wood structure. 
Mr. Son Le: It's the wood structure. I had to go to the Historical for that to make 
sure that there was not historic significance before I can get demo. 
Mr. Francis: There's nothing else to do. I mean he's filed it. We are reading. We 
are just waiting on the building. I was hoping to tell yon tonight we have the permit and we 
don't need to but - - -
Mr. Sergi: Well is somebody going to follow up with the building department. Are 
you or someone else going to follow up? 
3
Mr. Son Le: Yes, I just called earlier today and they said they are tall<lng to the 
commissioner about it and that's all I got. 
Mr. Sergi: Joe, do you have any questions? 
Mr. Attardo: No. 
Mr. Sergi: I don't have any other further questions and the board doesn't have any. 
Mr. Francis: And I understand again that this was the last one the last time but 
again had we not filed, I wouldn't be here today. 
Mr. Sergi: And you're asl<lng for another six month or what are you asl<lng for? 
Mr. Francis: If you want to grant shorter, we'll take less than. Six months is the 
standard so that's what we are asl<lng, but if you guys for some reason wanted to grant a 
shorter extension - I expect he'll have it within the next two weeks or a week or so, 
hopefully. So, again, if the board wanted to consider a shorter extension, I would 
understand. 
Mr. Sergi: I'll entertain a motion from the hoard if anyone wants to make a motion. 
On motion of Ms. Gelineau seconded by Mr. Taranto, the board voted to grant an 
extension for Case No. 2023-18. 
Mr. Sergi: For how long? 
Ms. Gelineau: Six months. 
4
Roll call: Mr. Taranto, yes; Ms. Gelineau, yes; Mr. Deveaux, yes; Mr. Attardo, yes; 
and Mr. Sergi: I'll vote yes but will you see if you can get this done, guys! I don't want to 
see you back here. 
Mr. Francis: Final, final! 
Mr. Sergi: The next case is Case No. 2026-21, Petitioner/Owner: Donald & Maureen 
DeBernadi. Will the clerk be kind enough to read the Petition please? 
The clerk then read the Petition in Case No. 2026-21, Petitioner/Owner: Donald & 
Maureen DeBernadi. Nature of Appeal/Petition: Variance. Subject Matter to allow for the 
construction of an attached.single-story garage (for an attached three-vehicle garage) 
located off the rear of the single-family home. Location and Zoning District: 50 
Wimbledon Circle; Residence A-2 Zoning District. Provisions of Zoning Ordinance 
Involved. Sections 4.11 - Rear and Side Yard Variances. Specific Relief Sought: Petitioner 
proposes an addition to the rear of the structure in the form of a single story three garage 
bay (for a total of three (3) vehicles and storage) that will sit 17 feet and 18.3 feet off the six­
yard lot lines and 16.5 feet off the rear-yard lot line. 
Mr. Sergi: Thank you Matt. May we hear from the Petitioner or the Petitioner's 
representative, please. 
Attorney Bret Francis, Law Office, 10 Hammer Street, Waltham came forward and 
submitted a copy of his brief to each member on the board. 
Mr. Francis: I am here tonight on behalf of the Petitioners, Don and Maureen 
DeBernadi. 
5
(Mr. Francis went on to read his brief into the record. He submitted drawings of 
what the extended garage would look like.) 
Mr. Francis: With that, I'll wrap up my presentation and answer any questions that 
the board may have. 
Mr. Sergi: Counselor, have you seen the communication from the City of 
Cambridge Water Department about the encroachments? 
Mr. Francis: I did. We've discussed them since then and, yes, they are there and he 
has agreed to remove them. Further I guess they were also looking for a survey done of the 
property, which, as you can, has been done. So we would agree to work with them in 
determining the borders of the property as well. I guess they wanted to replace some of the 
boundaries. So we are in agreement with all three of those. We'll remove the structures 
and we've done a survey and we'll work with the city with anything that they need on their 
end. 
Mr. Sergi: Do you want to add that to your decision? 
Mr. Francis: I can do that. I can give it to Pam in the morning. And if you have 
language you wanted to put in it, I will listen to it and accept it tonight. 
Mr. Sergi: No, I'd like your proposed language before the end of the night 
And the abutters on the other side are all set with this? 
Mr. Francis: They are here tonight. 
Mr. Sergi: I'll open it up to questions from the board. 
6
Mr. Sergi: Steve? 
Mr. Taranto: No, I have none. 
Mr. Sergi: Glenna? 
Ms. Gelineau: I'm just curious. You have a two car garage now and you're adding 
three? 
Mr. Francis: They are adding one to make it a total of three. And it's more for 
storage but there may be another vehicle as well. But a lot of it is actually related to the 
City of Cambridge. We're getting that stuff out of both the tent that they referred to. A lot 
of that is going into the garage. So this is actually to move that along. 
Ms. Gelineau: Oh, okay. 
Mr. Sergi: Matt, do you have any questions? 
Mr. Deveaux: No questions. 
Mr. Sergi: Joe? 
Mr. Attardo: I have no questions. 
Mr. Sergi: I don't have any further questions, so I'll open it up to the audience, 
Is there anyone in the audience that's against the petition as presented? 
Seeing none. Is there anyone seeking information? 
7
Seeing none. Is there anyone in favor of the petition that would like to have a show 
of hands? 
(Five people raised their hand in favor.) 
Mr. Sergi: Let me ask you, counselor, the Findings of Fact and the Decision that we 
have on file, have you made any changes? 
Mr. Francis: Other than the proposed ones I intend to make. They have been on 
file for about a month or more than a month and no changes have been made. 
Mr. Sergi: Why don't you take a stab at proposing those changes now. At lease we 
will have it on the record. 
Mr. Francis: The first one is to remove all structures. I mean one of them is a tent 
and one of them is a shed, so both of the structures will be removed. 
Number two, they wanted a survey done of the property which we had done for 
purposes of tonight and then three, we will absolutely cooperate with them regarding 
installation of the boundary markers and determination of boundaries. 
Mr. Sergi: Both three points you will add in the conditions in the decision. 
Mr. Francis: Yes. 
Mr. Deveaux: Let's do those three points again. Let's do 1, 2 and 3. 
Mr. Francis. 1. Remove all structures from the City of Cambridge Property. 
8
On motion of Ms. Gelineau, seconded by Mr. Taranto, the board voted that the 
Proposed Findings of Fact be the Findings of Fact of the board. 
Roll call: Mr. Taranto, yes; Ms. Gelineau, yes; Mr. Deveaux, yes; Mr. Attardo, yes 
and Mr. Sergi, yes. 
Mr. Sergi: In a similar fashion, I would entertain a motion of the Proposed 
Decision, as amended tonight, with the three additional conditions as outlined. 
On motion of Mr. Taranto, seconded by Ms. Gelineau, the board voted that the 
Proposed Decision, as amended tonight, be the decision of the board. 
Roll call: Mr. Taranto, yes; Ms. Gelineau, yes; Mr. Deveaux, yes; Mr. Attardo, yes 
and Mr. Sergi, yes. 
Mr. Sergi: It's been granted. Good luck! 
One more motion is in order. 
On motion of Mr. Deveaux, seconded by Mr. Taranto, the board voted to adjourn at 
7:21 P.M.
